passage:
During cooking class, Group Three was making vegetable soup. The recipe asked for one spoon of sugar, but Kevin added one spoon of salt by mistake. Then another student added the correct salt too.
The soup became too salty.
The group wanted to start over, but there were no extra vegetables. Their teacher suggested adding more water and potatoes. The soup was still salty, but much better.
At the end, Group Three wrote in their report: "Mistakes can sometimes be balanced, but it is easier to read carefully first."
The soup lesson was simple. Cooking, like many things, requires attention before action. Fixing a mistake can take more work than avoiding one.
